tier_reason: The README only repeats a '2-3 times faster than PARDISO' headline, but the bundled user guide (GSS 2.4 quick start, section 7, Table 1) gives first-party numeric-factorization times for 12 SuiteSparse (UF) matrices against Intel Composer XE 2013 SP1 PARDISO, naming CPU, GPU, CUDA version and OS. The library ships only as closed Windows binaries with no benchmark code or compiler flags, so the numbers are first-party and not reproducible: C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'For many large matrices, GSS is about 2-3 times faster than PARDISO and other CPU based solvers.' User guide Table 1 (numerical factorization time, s, GSS 2.4 CPU-GPU hybrid vs PARDISO): total 315.114 vs 904.244 over 12 matrices, about 2.9x (derived from page data); per matrix up to 5.4x on nd24k (15.880 vs 85.519) and 4.3x on Fault_639 (43.633 vs 186.405), but GSS is slower on msdoor (1.061 vs 0.424), inline_1 (3.385 vs 2.605) and boneS10 (5.585 vs 4.636). The guide itself says 'For matrices need short time computing, PARDISO is faster than GSS.'
corrections.workload: Numerical factorization time only (not symbolic analysis or solve) on 12 SuiteSparse/UF matrices (msdoor, inline_1, apache2, boneS10, audikw_1, bone010, StocF-1465, nd24k, Fault_639, Flan_1565, Emilia_923, nd12k), both solvers at default parameters; GSS 2.4 runs CPU-GPU hybrid, PARDISO runs CPU only.
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i7-4770 (3.4 GHz), 24 GB RAM, ASUS GTX 780 GPU (compute capability 3.5), CUDA Toolkit 5.5, Windows 7 64-bit (user guide section 7, dated 2014).
corrections.baseline: Intel MKL PARDISO (Intel Composer XE 2013 SP1), CPU only
corrections.caveats: Closed-source trial distribution: the repo holds only Windows x64 DLLs (GSS_Dl.dll, GrusLic_de.dll, cublas64_55.dll), a trial license file (gss_spd.lic), headers, C/Fortran samples and a PDF guide; no license grant, no source. The speedup compares a CPU+GPU hybrid run against CPU-only PARDISO on 2013-era hardware, covers numerical factorization only, and GSS loses on 3 of 12 matrices (smaller/shorter jobs). No benchmark harness or compiler flags are published, so the numbers cannot be reproduced. Built against CUDA 5.5. Last commit 2021-10-05; the benchmarked release (GSS 2.4) dates from 2014. The linked arXiv paper (2109.14929, Q-learning for sparse Gaussian elimination) is a preprint; it could not be opened from this environment.

notes: README alone has only the headline; the real numbers are in the user guide PDF inside the trial folder (Table 1, page 15), so benchmark_url now points there. The headline 2-3x holds for long-running matrices (sum ratio about 2.9x), but it is GPU-assisted GSS against CPU-only PARDISO, and PARDISO wins on short jobs. Metadata checked on github.com: 22 stars, 3 forks, 9 commits, not a fork, not archived, no license file; the grusoft.com comparison image and arxiv.org were not opened (arxiv.org is blocked by egress here).
